issues.detail: Missing guidance on error scenarios such as malformed allocations, empty variants, cache refresh failures, or null user IDs.
Provides code snippets but lacks end-to-end examples of targeting rule evaluation, database integration, and admin endpoint implementations.
All code examples are TypeScript-specific despite claiming compatibility with 'any backend language'; missing examples in Python, Go, or Java.
Examples describe scenarios and expected outputs but lack complete, working code demonstrating flag definitions and actual evaluation results.

scenarios.name: gradual-api-endpoint-rollout
scenarios.rationale: Response A fails the explicit rubric requirement for SHA-256 hashing by using MD5 instead, and hashes only userId rather than the required flagKey:userId combination; Response B correctly implements all three rubric items: boolean flag with 95/5 allocation, deterministic bucketing via SHA-256(flagKey:userId), and server-side middleware checking the enabled flag before variant assignment.

scenarios.name: targeted-multivariant-pricing-test
scenarios.rationale: Response A is a well-structured test methodology guide (hypothesis, metrics, sample size) but fails the rubric by omitting any flag definition, concrete targeting rules, and entirely missing deterministic bucketing demonstration. Response B directly implements all three rubric requirements: explicit multivariate flag with [33.33, 33.33, 33.34] allocation, targeting rules for country=US and plan=free, and deterministic bucketing via SHA256 hash to ensure consistent variant assignment per user.

scenarios.name: flag-lifecycle-and-stale-flag-monitoring
scenarios.rationale: Response A provides no implementation of any rubric requirement, only clarifying questions; Response B implements all three (archiving, logging structure, monitoring) with working code and thorough detail, but uses a PATCH endpoint instead of the DELETE method explicitly specified in the rubric.
